clue.text: The moon is edam ultimately — strange form of belief!

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of order, so the letters of the first three words are rearranged
ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter of the cheese is taken

explanation.surface: A whimsical claim that the moon is made of cheese is called a peculiar creed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges THE MOON IS; 'ultimately' adds the last letter of 'edam', M, at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Belief in a single god is a particular kind of religious faith, hence a form of belief.

clue.text: Animals packed into box, endangered

indicators.note: packed into says the answer sits tucked inside the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Livestock crammed into a crate are at risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packed into' shows the letters lie inside 'box, endangered', across the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural cattle used as draught beasts are animals.

clue.text: Object to there being nothing on m-model

parts.note: nothing is the round figure zero, letter O
a stammered model, here pose (to model) said with a stutter on its first letter

explanation.surface: A speaker stammers while protesting that someone is posing with nothing on.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'm-model' signals a stutter: the synonym for model, POSE, is given the same stammered start, P-POSE. In a down clue 'on' places O above it.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppose something is to raise an objection to it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Homer is out to demonstrate courage

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A remark that the poet Homer sets out to show bravery in his epics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges HOMER IS; 'to demonstrate' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroism is bravery shown in action, a synonym of courage.

clue.text: Metal particle that's right inside

indicators.note: inside says the letter for right goes within the particle

parts.note: an ion is a charged atomic particle

explanation.surface: Something about a tiny piece of metal with the correct thing in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron is a common metallic element, so it is an example of a metal.

clue.text: Keep an eye on silly moron drinking vermouth

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the drink goes inside the jumbled letters
silly suggests the letters of the insult are jumbled foolishly

parts.note: IT is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: Watch out for that foolish idiot knocking back vermouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' gives MONOR, which 'drinking' opens up. IT for Italian vermouth comes from the British bar order gin and it.
explanation.definitionFit: To monitor something is to observe and check it over time, so to keep watch on it.

clue.text: Oil flowing into cellar

indicators.note: flowing suggests liquid movement, so the letters run into a new order

explanation.surface: Oil is pouring down into the basement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowing' rearranges INTO CELLAR to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Citronella is an aromatic oil from a grass, used to keep insects away.

clue.text: Goon messed about? Gosh!

indicators.note: about means scattered around, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise on finding a buffoon has been fooling around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges GOON MESSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise, used interchangeably.

clue.text: There's nothing to gain, being an alcoholic

parts.note: to gain a prize is to win it
nothing is zero, letter O

explanation.surface: Someone says drinking heavily brings no profit.
explanation.definitionFit: A wino is slang for someone addicted to drink, especially cheap wine.

clue.text: Sergeant has problem with foot, a trifling thing

parts.note: Sergeant Pepper, from the Beatles album title
a corn is a painful patch of hard skin on the foot

explanation.surface: An army sergeant suffers from a sore foot, a minor matter.
explanation.walkthrough: A peppercorn rent is a nominal sum paid, so the word stands for anything insignificant.
explanation.definitionFit: From the token peppercorn rent, the word means something of negligible value.

clue.text: Woman at home must join network

parts.note: being in means being at home
a grid is a network, as in the electricity grid

explanation.surface: A lady staying at home must connect to the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrid is a woman's first name, as in the actress Ingrid Bergman.

clue.text: Food on a street in distant countries

parts.note: fare is food served, as in plain fare

explanation.surface: Street food found in faraway lands.
explanation.definitionFit: The countries of East Asia, remote from Europe, are collectively called by this name.

clue.text: Gangster getting close in rural homestead? Nothing to worry about!

indicators.note: in places the gangster and the closing word within the homestead

parts.note: a farm is a homestead in the country
Al Capone, the famous gangster, gives AL
to seal something is to close it up

explanation.surface: A mobster gets near a country farmhouse, but it turns out there was no threat.
explanation.definitionFit: A warning that proves unfounded means there was no real danger after all.

clue.text: The one of one is one

definitions.text: The one of one is one

parts.words: The one of one is one
parts.note: read mathematically: the number that, multiplied by one, gives one is itself one, so the inverse of unity is unity

explanation.surface: A riddling statement about the number one.
explanation.walkthrough: One over one is one: the multiplicative inverse of 1 is 1.
explanation.definitionFit: The multiplicative inverse of a number is one divided by it, and for unity that inverse equals unity.

clue.text: Tribe's original language using few words

indicators.note: original means the first, so only the opening letter of the tribe is used

parts.note: Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland or Scotland

explanation.surface: A tribe's native tongue is said to be brief and clipped.
explanation.walkthrough: ERSE, the Gaelic language, is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse speech is brief and curt, expressed with few words.

clue.text: Exciting quality that Cameron could offer

indicators.note: the letters of the politician's name could offer, when rearranged, another word

explanation.surface: Political commentary on the glamour David Cameron might bring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could offer' is a loose anagram signal: CAMERON rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Romance is a sense of glamour, mystery and excitement surrounding something.

clue.text: Lots of paper getting left in area

indicators.note: in puts the letter for left within the paper quantity

parts.note: a ream is a large quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: Huge amounts of paper are abandoned in some district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside REAM: REA-L-M.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a field or domain, as in the realm of science, so an area.

clue.text: Visitors to Buckingham Palace may have poetic quality

parts.words: Visitors to Buckingham Palace may have
parts.note: guests at the palace may have met ER, the Queen (Elizabeth Regina) who lived there

parts.words: Visitors to Buckingham Palace may have
parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen in residence at the palace

explanation.surface: Guests at Buckingham Palace may come away with a lyrical air.
explanation.walkthrough: Buckingham Palace is the London home of the British monarch; ER is Queen Elizabeth. The answer is the American spelling of metre.
explanation.definitionFit: Meter, the US spelling of metre, is the rhythmic pattern of verse, a quality of poetry.

clue.text: Ex England cricketer or rugby player

definitions.meaning: Tony ..., a spin bowler who played Test cricket for England
a second-row forward in a rugby scrum has this positional name

explanation.surface: A sports question: a former England cricketer or someone who plays rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Lock was an England spin bowler of the 1950s and 60s; in rugby the position is in the second row of the scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name a person: a specific former Test cricketer and a rugby forward position.

clue.text: Place America in an advantage

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street addresses
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: Putting America in a favourable position.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is a benefit or point in favour, hence an advantage.

clue.text: Song when Sarah is embraced by her husband!

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside, so the name goes within the husband's title

parts.note: Sarah Brown's husband Gordon Brown was Prime Minister when this appeared, abbreviated PM
Sal is a familiar short form of Sarah

explanation.surface: A tender scene in which a woman is hugged by her husband and a song is sung.
explanation.walkthrough: When this puzzle appeared, Gordon Brown was the UK Prime Minister and his wife was named Sarah, so 'her husband' points to his title.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a sacred song or hymn, such as those in the Book of Psalms.

clue.text: Someone making a dash, heading off to get computer accessory

indicators.note: heading off means the head, or first letter, is removed

parts.note: a sprinter runs a dash, a short fast race

explanation.surface: A runner sets off in a hurry to fetch a gadget for a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the first letter of SPRINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A printer is a device connected to a computer to produce paper copies, a peripheral.

clue.text: Excellent fellow, male leading old kingdom

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so the letter for male comes first

parts.note: ace means excellent, as in an ace performance
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A fine chap, a man in charge of an ancient realm.
explanation.definitionFit: Macedon was an ancient kingdom of northern Greece, ruled by Alexander the Great.

clue.text: Check out old stories about leader of party

indicators.note: about means around, so the old stories surround the party letter

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife
lore is a body of traditional stories

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Investigate ancient tales about the head of a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the two-piece charade around the party letter rather than around one piece alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To explore something is to investigate or examine it, to check it out.

clue.text: Ornamental work showing sheep in club

indicators.note: in places the sheep inside the club

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club used as a weapon
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Decorative handiwork depicting a sheep at a club meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Macrame is decorative knotted string or cord work, a form of ornamental craft.

clue.text: Deliver a coat

definitions.meaning: to hand over or give, as in delivering a verdict or a service
a layer of plaster or cement applied to a wall

explanation.surface: An instruction to hand over a jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to give or provide; the other is a plaster finish applied in a coat.

clue.text: Gents perhaps needing money to relax

parts.note: the gents is a men's toilet, an example of a loo
the sen is a small unit of money in Japan and elsewhere in Asia

explanation.surface: Someone needs cash to use a public toilet and unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: The gents is the British term for a men's public toilet. SEN, a small Asian coin, is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: To loosen is to make less tight or rigid, a synonym of relax.

clue.text: Bluster of second-rate newspaper

parts.note: B grade is second-rate, after A
a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: Bombast from a poor-quality tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluster and brag both mean boastful, self-important talk.

clue.text: Garments he's discarded, the fool!

indicators.note: discarded means thrown away, so the letters of he's are removed

parts.note: clothes are garments

explanation.surface: An idiot has thrown off his clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discarded' removes HES (from 'he's') from CLOTHES.
explanation.definitionFit: Clot is British slang for a stupid person, a fool.

clue.text: Nonsense from sailor, a cheat

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
to diddle someone is to swindle or cheat them

explanation.surface: Rubbish talk from a seaman who is a swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: Taradiddle means pretentious nonsense or a petty lie, a dated term for rubbish talk.

clue.text: Reagan bestriding a horse

indicators.note: bestriding means straddling, so the name sits around the letter

parts.note: Ronald Reagan, US president, gives the short name Ron

explanation.surface: Ronald Reagan, a former cowboy actor, sitting astride a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Reagan, a former Hollywood cowboy actor, suits a picture of riding astride.
explanation.definitionFit: A roan is a horse with a coat of mixed coloured and white hairs.

clue.text: Greek character, breaker of promise, about to be spritually reborn

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the whole run of letters reads backwards

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a reneger is someone who goes back on a promise

explanation.surface: A Greek promise-breaker is on the point of a religious conversion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ETA plus RENEGER backwards as one string. 'spritually' is the clue's misspelling of spiritually.
explanation.definitionFit: To regenerate in the religious sense is to be born again in spirit.
